skill.name: convex-explain-app
skill.description: Explains an existing Convex application from its schema and function surface, including relationships, access boundaries, authentication, components, external edges, and request flows.
skill.summary: Create a source-grounded architecture map of an existing Convex application without changing it.
skill.author: get-convex

content.value_statement: Understanding an unfamiliar Convex application requires connecting schemas, functions, authentication, and integrations. This skill produces a structured, source-grounded architecture map without modifying the application.
actual_capabilities: Maps Convex tables, fields, relationships, and indexes from the application schema.
Separates public functions from internal functions and summarizes their data access.
Describes identity establishment and ownership enforcement shown in the source.
Identifies installed Convex components, HTTP routes, cron jobs, external APIs, and environment variable references.
Traces representative request flows and presents the results as a scannable architecture map.
limitations: It describes observed architecture but does not perform a complete security audit.
It does not modify source files, deployments, schemas, or application data.
Its accuracy depends on access to the schema and complete function surface.
It reports ambiguous behavior when the available source does not establish a clear conclusion.

use_cases.title: Onboard to a Convex codebase
use_cases.description: Build a concise map of tables, functions, authentication, integrations, and request flows before making changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare architecture documentation
use_cases.description: Turn the current schema and function surface into source-grounded documentation for technical review.

use_cases.title: Scope a deeper review
use_cases.description: Identify public surfaces, ownership patterns, and external edges that deserve focused security or readiness analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the application
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain this Convex application using its schema and exported functions. Summarize tables, relationships, public functions, internal functions, and authentication.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for a first overview of an unfamiliar project.

prompt_templates.title: Map data and access
prompt_templates.prompt: Map every Convex table, relationship, index, and function. Show which public and internal functions read or write each table.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when planning a feature that depends on existing data.

prompt_templates.title: Trace system flows
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain authentication, ownership checks, components, HTTP routes, cron jobs, and external calls. Trace two representative requests from entry point to data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this to understand boundaries and runtime behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Produce an architecture handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a source-grounded Convex architecture handoff. Highlight ambiguous behavior, public exposure, data relationships, ownership enforcement, external edges, and recommended next review steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this before a security review, migration, or major extension.

output_examples.input: Explain the data model and relationships in this task application.
output_examples.output: The application stores projects, tasks, and users. Tasks belong to projects through projectId and to users through ownerId.

output_examples.input: Which functions are client-accessible, and what data do they touch?
output: Public queries read projects and tasks for the authenticated user.
Public mutations create and update tasks after ownership checks.
Internal functions perform maintenance work and are not directly client-accessible.

output_examples.output: The client calls createTask, identity is verified, ownership is checked, and the task is inserted before listMyTasks reads it by index.

best_practices: Provide the complete Convex schema and function surface for the most accurate map.
Ask the skill to identify uncertainty whenever generated files or deployment details are unavailable.
Follow the architecture map with a dedicated authorization or launch-readiness review.
anti_patterns: Do not treat descriptive output as proof that authorization is secure.
Do not request inferred behavior when the source does not show it.
Do not use an outdated schema or partial function list as the sole source of truth.

faq.question: Does this skill change my Convex application?
faq.answer: No. It reads available source and deployment metadata to produce documentation.

faq.question: What source files does it use?
faq.answer: It relies on the Convex schema, exported function surface, authentication configuration, component configuration, HTTP routes, and cron definitions.

faq.question: Can it inspect a deployed application?
faq.answer: Yes, when official read-only deployment tools are available. Otherwise, it analyzes the local source.

faq.question: Does it audit authorization vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It describes authentication and ownership patterns, then recommends a dedicated authorization review.

faq.question: How does it handle missing information?
faq.answer: It marks unclear behavior as ambiguous instead of inventing an explanation.

faq.question: What does the final output contain?
faq.answer: The output covers data relationships, function visibility, authentication, ownership, components, external edges, representative flows, and appropriate next review steps.
